verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is designed to last approximately 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "a more than 600,000-mile, 10-day journey" (R1); "685,000 mile, 10-day journey" (R2); "10-day mission" (multiple)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the mission duration as 10 days or approximately 10 days.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission has a four-person crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "four astronauts" (R1, R2, R3, etc.); lists Wiseman, Glover, Koch, Hansen
verifications.reasoning: All sources consistently describe a crew of four astronauts.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will journey around the Moon and return to Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "journey around the moon and back to Earth" (R1, R4); "around the moon, also known as a lunar fly-by" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported as a lunar flyby mission returning to Earth.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is launching on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "April 1 between 6:24 p.m. ET" (R1); "blasted off ... on Wednesday evening" (April 1, R3); "lifted off ... at 6:35 p.m. EDT" (R4)

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a crewed flight.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first time humans have traveled beyond low Earth orbit" (R1); "four-person crew" (all)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly described as the first crewed Artemis mission.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will test Orion's systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "test critical spacecraft systems" (R1); "test Orion’s systems" (R2); "check that the spacecraft can safely make the journey" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Primary objective is testing Orion and related systems.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission has a planned splashdown in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashdown ... Pacific Ocean on April 10" (R3); "Splashdown in the Pacific Ocean" (R5); "April 11, 2026, 00:07:27 UTC (April 10, 5:07:27 p.m. PDT)" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Pacific Ocean splashdown on April 10 local time.

verifications.claim: As of April 1, 2026, the Artemis II mission is approximately 5 hours 29 minutes into it.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No source mentions the mission being exactly 5 hours 29 minutes into it as of April 1.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission goal is a crewed "free return" trajectory loop around the far side of the Moon and back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "free-return trajectory" (R2, R5); "fly by the far side of the moon" (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Described as crewed free-return trajectory around the far side.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission reaches a maximum distance of over 250,000 miles from Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm maximum distance exceeds 250,000 miles.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will take around three to four days to reach the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "three days to get to the moon" (R1); "around three days" (R2); "Four-day trip to the Moon" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources state three or four days outbound, matching 'around three to four'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will perform a lunar flyby.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as a lunar flyby mission.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will take another four days to return to Earth.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.reasoning: Sources vary between three and four days for return; claim specifies four, supported but not precisely by all.

verifications.claim: The Artemis I mission was uncrewed.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "uncrewed Artemis I test flight" (R1); "uncrewed Orion spacecraft" (R6)

verifications.claim: The Artemis I mission took place in 2022.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.claim: The Artemis I mission was a three-week mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "over the course of about a three-week mission"; "Mission duration: 25 days"
verifications.reasoning: Described as about three weeks (25 days ≈ 3.5 weeks, but source uses 'three-week').

verifications.claim: The Artemis I mission was longer than the Artemis II mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Artemis I: 25 days (R6); Artemis II: 10 days / 9 days 1 hour (R1, R7)

verifications.claim: The Artemis I mission focused on testing the SLS rocket and Orion capsule in deep space
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first integrated flight test of ... Orion spacecraft, Space Launch System (SLS) rocket ... in deep space"
